prerequisites: Termodinámica Química Aplicada a la Ingeniería
Cinética y Reactores Químicos (Chemical Kinetics part)

learning_outcomes.text: Perform all phases present in the execution of a correct physicochemical experiment: design, sample preparation, data collection, graphical representation and mathematical treatment of data, calculation of measurement errors and propagated errors, and analysis of results.
Correctly handle a set of complex instruments.
Solve typical problems of substance identification from measured properties.
Prepare and correctly present a report, both orally and in writing, corresponding to one of the practices carried out in the physicochemical characterization laboratory.

syllabus_topics: Determination and application of visible-ultraviolet spectra.
Identification of organic substances using FTIR.
Determination of adsorption isotherms on activated carbon.
Determination of properties of a weak acid by electrical conductivity measurements.
teaching_methods: Classroom Practice sessions (seminars on experimental error calculation, technical report elaboration, oral presentation strategies, lab notebook elaboration, hygiene and safety rules, experiment introduction)

Laboratory Practice sessions (pre-reading test, explanation of experiment fundamentals, personalized group follow-up, experimental work, data collection, data and error treatment, lab notebook supervision)
Group report/memory elaboration and oral defense
Use of computational resources (Excel, Python interactive notebooks)

assessment_methods.method: Written exam with questions and problems
Continuous evaluation sheet (lab work, organization, instrument handling, understanding, pre-reading test, lab notebook quality)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, an overall final grade of at least 5.0 is required, along with a minimum of 4.0 in the final exam (F) and 5.0 in the oral and written report (IOE). If these minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as 0.4*F + 0.3*IOE + 0.3*EC. If the final exam is failed in the ordinary call, but IOE and EC are passed, a new final exam (F') is taken for the extraordinary call, with the grade calculated as 0.4*F' + 0.3*IOE + 0.3*EC. If the report or continuous evaluation is failed, a new final exam (F') and a lab practice exam (PL) are taken, with PL having a minimum of 5.0 and a 60% weight, calculated as 0.4*F' + 0.6*PL. All experimental sessions must be completed.
